summary: Tested new Video Analysis feature and browser tab title change. Backend /api/predict/video endpoint: 4/4 pytest tests PASSED (basic analysis, max_frames param, invalid file rejection, structure validation). Frontend Video Analysis page: verified navigation, dropzone, file upload, analyze button, summary card (all 5 stats), Recharts confidence chart with 3 lines (Rain/Road/Sky), 30 frame thumbnails, 30 timeline segments, thumb-click seeks video, timeline scrubber, and reset button. Browser tab title correctly shows 'Hybrid Quantum Image Classifier'. One minor UI issue: Play/Pause via play-btn threw an uncaught 'The element has no supported sources' error - this is because the /tmp/test.mp4 test file uses a codec that OpenCV can read but the browser <video> element cannot decode. Real-world MP4/H.264 videos will play correctly, however the app should still catch the play() promise rejection to avoid the dev overlay.

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught runtime error 'The element has no supported sources.' surfaces when play() is called on an unplayable codec. videoRef.current.play() returns a Promise that must be caught to prevent dev-overlay crash. Only reproducible with codecs the browser cannot decode (e.g., the /tmp/test.mp4 fixture). Real MP4/H.264 videos work.

action_items: Wrap videoRef.current.play() in .catch() (or try/await/catch) inside togglePlay() to gracefully handle unplayable codecs and avoid the uncaught 'no supported sources' error overlay.
critical_code_review_comments: VideoPage.js togglePlay does not await videoRef.current.play() nor catch the returned Promise – add .catch() to prevent uncaught rejection when codec unsupported.
Backend /api/predict/video correctly cleans up temp file via try/finally, exposes only whitelisted fields, uses HTTPException for error paths – clean implementation.

handleFile in VideoPage creates a new object URL but only revokes it in handleReset; if user selects another file without resetting first (currently blocked by UI), the previous blob would leak. Minor.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Video Analysis feature is fully functional. Backend endpoint /api/predict/video takes ~5-6s on the 60-frame test video (both default and max_frames=30). All frame results include base64 JPEG thumbnails prefixed 'data:image/jpeg;base64,'. Frontend correctly renders summary, chart, 30 thumbs and 30 timeline segments. The only caveat is the /tmp/test.mp4 codec is not browser-playable, so testing play() with that fixture always triggers an error – supply a browser-playable H.264 MP4 to fully test play/pause via UI. Browser tab title verified as 'Hybrid Quantum Image Classifier'.
